officialTitle: First-Line Atezolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.notes: Four 21-day cycles of carboplatin-etoposide with atezolizumab or placebo (induction), then maintenance atezolizumab or placebo. PD-L1 testing not required for enrolment. 201 patients assigned to atezolizumab and 202 to placebo.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding atezolizumab to carboplatin-etoposide improve survival in untreated extensive-stage SCLC?

pico.population: Previously untreated extensive-stage SCLC, unselected for PD-L1
pico.intervention: Atezolizumab plus carboplatin-etoposide, then maintenance atezolizumab
pico.comparator: Placebo plus carboplatin-etoposide, then maintenance placebo
pico.outcomes: Co-primary: investigator-assessed PFS and OS (ITT). Safety

arms.label: Atezolizumab + CP/ET
arms.regimen: Atezolizumab + carboplatin + etoposide, then atezolizumab maintenance
arms.dosing: Carboplatin AUC 5 day 1, etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3, atezolizumab 1,200 mg IV day 1, every 21 days for four cycles, then maintenance atezolizumab
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients with untreated ES-SCLC were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive four 21-day cycles of CP (area under the curve 5 mg per mL/min intravenously [IV], day 1) plus ET (100 mg/mIV, days 1-3) with atezolizumab (1,200 mg IV, day 1) or placebo, and then maintenance atezolizumab or placebo until unacceptable toxicity, disease progression, or loss of clinical benefit.

arms.label: Placebo + CP/ET
arms.regimen: Placebo + carboplatin + etoposide, then placebo maintenance

publications.title: First-Line Atezolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary (interim) analysis

publications.title: Updated Overall Survival and PD-L1 Subgroup Analysis of Patients With Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer Treated With Atezolizumab, Carboplatin, and Etoposide (IMpower133).
publications.label: Updated OS analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: At a median follow-up of 13.9 months, the median overall survival was 12.3 months in the atezolizumab group and 10.3 months in the placebo group (hazard ratio for death, 0.70; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.54 to 0.91; P=0.007).
The median progression-free survival was 5.2 months and 4.3 months, respectively (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.96; P=0.02).

At the updated analysis, median follow-up for OS was 22.9 months; 302 deaths had occurred. Median OS was 12.3 and 10.3 months with atezolizumab plus CP/ET and placebo plus CP/ET, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.95; descriptive= .0154). At 18 months, 34.0% and 21.0% of patients were alive in atezolizumab plus CP/ET and placebo plus CP/ET arms, respectively.

safety.description: Safety consistent with known profiles of individual agents; no new findings (no numbers in abstract)
safety.sourceQuote: The safety profile of atezolizumab plus carboplatin and etoposide was consistent with the previously reported safety profile of the individual agents, with no new findings observed.

strengths: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised phase III design
Both co-primary endpoints met; OS benefit maintained at updated analysis
limitations: Modest absolute gain in median OS and PFS
Prophylactic thoracic radiotherapy was not part of the protocol, so the interaction with consolidative thoracic radiotherapy is unknown
Benefit observed regardless of PD-L1 or bTMB in exploratory analyses; no predictive biomarker identified

clinicalImplications.text: Established atezolizumab plus carboplatin-etoposide followed by atezolizumab maintenance as a first-line standard for extensive-stage SCLC, without biomarker selection.

tumourBoardPearl.text: No PD-L1 or TMB test is needed to select patients for first-line chemo-immunotherapy in extensive-stage SCLC; benefit appeared biomarker-independent.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMID 30280641 (primary) and PMID 33439693 (updated OS; source of dosing quote). The updated report describes the study as phase I/III.
